findings: Zen5 direct16 is direction-branchy; direct32 uses two cmovb selections per comparison. Both scalar consumers unroll two sequential queries. No SIMD/gathers/calls.

Granite direct16 and direct32 both use direction branches, one query at a time. Direct16 adds three instructions per comparison path and a per-probe scalar count reload; direct32 retains a per-probe extent endpoint compare from memory.

For each method on each architecture, entire captured x86-v3/v4 function opcode bytes are identical. Function placement may differ; timing ISA labels do not establish an AVX512 effect in these kernels.
Direct32 is a necessary reverse baseline. The strong Zen5 baseline is direct32, while Granite blocked sparse widths8 remains competitive with both direct geometries in this particular trace.
These are codegen differences and measured associations, not identified microarchitectural causes. No matched forced-lowering experiment or branch PMU exists in this capture.
Blocked query reuse and changed before/after-soft physical offsets retain the limits recorded in the c9g audit.
scope: Read-only review of verified captured binaries and CSVs. Selectively fetched immutable asm/binaries; no source changes, builds, benchmark runs or worker launches.
